title: Shifted Composite Comparison
statement:
Canonical section variables and instances are those of the attached Lean module.

theorem shifted_composite_comparison
    {C D E : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category E]
    [HasShift C ℤ] [HasShift D ℤ] [HasShift E ℤ]
    (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) (H : C ⥤ E)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [G.CommShift ℤ] [H.CommShift ℤ]
    (c : H ⟶ F ⋙ G) [NatTrans.CommShift c ℤ]
    (X : C) (Y : D) (Z : E) (e : F.obj X ⟶ Y) (e' : G.obj Y ⟶ Z)
    (e'' : H.obj X ⟶ Z) (he : c.app X ≫ G.map e ≫ e' = e'') (n : ℤ) :
    c.app (X⟦n⟧) ≫
        G.map ((F.commShiftIso n).hom.app X ≫ e⟦n⟧') ≫
        (G.commShiftIso n).hom.app Y ≫ e'⟦n⟧' =
      (H.commShiftIso n).hom.app X ≫ e''⟦n⟧'

proof.text: Apply the shift functor to the unshifted composition equation. Naturality of the shift-commutation isomorphism moves the coefficient comparison through the shift; the composite-functor commutation law identifies the resulting composite with the shifted compositor.
